situation:
You are the marketing manager for RIDGELINE ADAPTIVE, a company that builds racing wheelchairs, handcycles and adaptive ski rigs. The business was founded by the grandfather of the owner (judge), and the owner (judge) is the third generation of the family to run it. The owner (judge) has asked you to recommend how the company should promote a new product bundle before the racing season opens.

Two seasons ago the company began pairing its equipment with sports nutrition, and it signed a supply agreement with a nutrition supplier that commits RIDGELINE ADAPTIVE to sell a full season's order of energy bars and hydration mixes. The company's own order records show a steady shift in what its athletes eat: less sugar, more plant-based protein, and smaller portions taken during training rather than after it.

RIDGELINE ADAPTIVE monitors open rates, click rates and unsubscribe rates on every message it sends. Those records point to roughly four thousand customers who have bought equipment in the past eighteen months. A mentor who advised the father of the owner (judge) for years disagrees with the records. He argues the company should rent an outside list of sixty thousand names and send the bundle offer to everyone on it, because the rented list costs almost nothing.

The rented list is cheap, but the company's email provider suspends senders whose complaint rate climbs, and a suspension would cut off the subscribers RIDGELINE ADAPTIVE already has. Sending only to the four thousand engaged customers means paying for an upgraded email platform that would consume what remains of the quarter's marketing budget, and it reaches far fewer buyers, which delays the revenue the supply agreement depends on.

The owner (judge) wants you to decide which information should drive this decision, to recommend one of the two approaches, and to explain how the bundle should be built and offered. The owner (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and after you have presented and answered questions, the owner (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the owner (judge) of RIDGELINE ADAPTIVE and the third generation of your family to run it. Business background is the same as the situation above. You have asked your marketing manager to tell you which information should drive this decision — the company's own order and email records, or the advice of the mentor who worked with your father — and to recommend either the rented list of sixty thousand names or the upgraded platform and the four thousand engaged customers. You also want to hear how the bundle itself should be built and offered.

You will greet the participant and ask to hear their ideas. After the participant has presented, ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: What are the first steps you would take to put this in place?
Who here would have to do what, and by when?
